answer: In PoA, remote attestation lets verifiers check that an agent runs approved enclave code by validating its MRENCLAVE and hardware-backed evidence; a registry must also bind identities to platform credentials and enforce its issuance policy. This raises Sybil costs: copying a VM cannot forge silicon-backed credentials, though MRENCLAVE alone is not unique and does not prevent multiple enclaves on one machine. Atlas, knoll, and prism can label policy profiles, not serve as security proofs.
